Assess Replication Outcomes Based on Various Criteria

assess_replication_outcome.Rd

This function evaluates the outcomes of replication studies against the original studies using various statistical criteria (see below, and vignette("success_criteria") for more details).

Usage

assess_replication_outcome(
  es_o,
  n_o,
  es_r,
  n_r,
  criterion,
  reported_success = NULL,
  result = NULL,
  pval_value_o = NULL,
  pval_type_o = NULL,
  pval_value_r = NULL,
  pval_type_r = NULL,
  pval_tails_o = NULL,
  pval_tails_r = NULL
)

Arguments

es_o

Numeric. The effect size from the original study.

n_o

Integer. The sample size of the original study.

es_r

Numeric. The effect size from the replication study.

n_r

Integer. The sample size of the replication study.

criterion

Character. The criterion to use for assessing the replication outcome. Options include: "significance_r", "significance_agg", "consistency_ci", "consistency_pi", "homogeneity", "homogeneity_significance", "small_telescopes" and "reported_success".

reported_success

Character. The outcome reported for each replication, as coded in the reported_success variable of the FReD dataset. Required when criterion = "reported_success", and ignored otherwise.

result

Character. Optional fallback for criterion = "reported_success", used where reported_success is missing: the result variable returned by load_fred_data().

pval_value_o

Numeric (or numeric string). Optional coded p-values for the original study (the pval_value_o column of FReD). Opt-in: used by "significance_r" and "homogeneity_significance" when supplied, falling back to p_from_r(es_o, n_o) where missing or indeterminate.

pval_type_o

Character. Optional inequality type labels for pval_value_o (e.g., "l (<)", "e (=)", "g (>)", "ge (>=)", "le (<=)"). Defaults to exact equality ("=") when omitted.

pval_value_r

Numeric (or numeric string). Optional coded p-values for the replication study (the pval_value_r column of FReD). Opt-in: used by "significance_r" when supplied, falling back to p_from_r(es_r, n_r) where missing or indeterminate.

pval_type_r

Character. Optional inequality type labels for pval_value_r. Defaults to exact equality ("=") when omitted.

pval_tails_o

Character or numeric. Optional tail specification for pval_value_o (the pval_tails_o column of FReD, e.g., "1 (one)" vs "2 (two)"). One-tailed p-values are doubled (pmin(2 * p, 1)) before comparing against two-tailed alpha = 0.05; omitted or missing values are treated as two-tailed.

pval_tails_r

Character or numeric. Optional tail specification for pval_value_r (the pval_tails_r column of FReD). Handled identically to pval_tails_o.

Value

A data frame with the outcome of the assessment based on the specified criterion, with three columns: outcome (success, failure or 'OS not significant'), outcome_detailed (a specific description of the criterion) and outcome_report (usually the same as outcome, but further broken out where there are distinct reasons for failure). For criterion = "reported_success", all three columns contain the reported label.

Details

The function assesses the replication outcome using one of several criteria:

significance_r

Evaluates the statistical significance of the replication effect (and whether its direction is consistent with the original effect). If the original study was not significant, this is highlighted as "OS not significant" (even if the replication effect size is missing, since the criterion is already meaningless). Coded p-values (pval_value_o/pval_value_r, with optional pval_type_* and pval_tails_*) are opt-in: when omitted (the default, used by the FReD Explorer), significance is computed solely from es and n via two-tailed p_from_r(). When supplied, coded p-values are evaluated first (with one-tailed values doubled to the two-tailed scale) and p_from_r() is used as a fallback wherever a coded p-value is missing or indeterminate at alpha = 0.05.

significance_agg

Aggregates the effect sizes from the original and replication studies using a meta-analytic approach and assesses whether the combined effect is significantly different from zero.

consistency_ci

Checks whether the original effect size falls within the confidence interval of the replication effect size, thus assessing consistency between the original and replication findings.

consistency_pi

Evaluates whether the replication effect size falls within the prediction interval derived from the original study and the size of the replication sample. This accounts for the expected variability in replication results.

homogeneity

Assesses whether the effects from the original and replication studies are homogeneous (i.e., consistent) using a heterogeneity test (Q-test).

homogeneity_significance

Combines the assessment of homogeneity with the significance of the effect sizes. It checks whether the two effects are homogeneous and jointly significantly different from zero. Because this criterion requires comparing both studies, rows with missing replication data return NA rather than "OS not significant".

small_telescopes

Tests whether the replication effect size is larger than the effect size that would have given the original study a power of 33%. Derived from Simonsohn (2015), the idea here is that replications should only count as successful if they indicate that the original study provided evidence (rather than a lucky guess).

reported_success

Uses the outcome as described by the replication authors instead of calculating one from effect sizes, so the effect size and sample size arguments do not affect it. Coded labels are returned unchanged (e.g., "successful", "failed", "mixed"). Where no outcome is coded, result is used, and "Not calculable" if that is missing as well.

Examples

es_o <- 0.3  # Effect size from the original study
n_o <- 100   # Sample size of the original study
es_r <- 0.25 # Effect size from the replication study
n_r <- 120   # Sample size of the replication study
assess_replication_outcome(es_o, n_o, es_r, n_r, "significance_r")
#>   outcome                  outcome_detailed outcome_report
#> 1 success replication effect is significant        success
assess_replication_outcome(es_o, n_o, es_r, n_r, "reported_success", reported_success = "mixed")
#>   outcome outcome_detailed outcome_report
#> 1   mixed            mixed          mixed
